text.p: A spokesman of French pharmaceuticals group Sanofi denied on Friday market rumours of a link-up with Synthelabo.
The spokesman said he "formally denies the rumours on the bourse of a link-up with Synthelabo".
Market talk centred on an imminent exchange of shares on a one-for-one basis between the two companies and the sale of Sanofi's beauty products division to l'Oreal, Synthelabo's parent, traders said.
Sanofi is the pharmaceuticals unit of Elf Aquitaine.
The Sanofi spokesman, who could not explain the sharp rise in its share price, said no announcements were planned this weekend, denying market talk to this effect.
Sanofi shares hit a high of 576 francs before giving up some gains to close up 6.17 percent at 568 francs on volume of 458,511 shares.
Synthelabo hit 577 francs before closing up 1.09 percent at 557 francs, while L'Oreal, which owns 57 percent of Synthelabo, eased 1.63 percent to 1,930 after a low of 1,902.
Traders pointed to the runup in Sanofi shares and trading volume around 1500 GMT, with some thinking U.S. investors were behind the move.
"There's no smoke without fire," said one market operator.
Pharmaceuticals have often led the gains on the Paris bourse since Elf recently said it was ready to give up its majority stake in Sanofi.
